text: The author concedes an arbitrage attack is feasible when experts fail to police their expertise and a significant share of the technically fungible tokens is offered on an exchange, since a malicious actor can then buy 51 percent of the tokens, vote against common sense, and sell before the tokens lose value.
citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vlad Andrei, Blockchain Infrastructure for Measuring Domain Specific Reputation in Autonomous Decentralized and A (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3125822

isBasedOn.name: Blockchain Infrastructure for Measuring Domain Specific Reputation in Autonomous Decentralized and A

abstract: However, it is feasible that an arbitrage opportunity could evolve if the experts do not police their expertise. If a significant percentage of the (technically fungible) tokens were put on sale in a token exchange, a malicious actor would have the opportunity to 1) buy 51% of tokens

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: requires expert policing to be absent
requires a liquid exchange holding a large share of tokens
